# Changelog

## 0.2.0

### Mini App hosting

The bot's Mini App can now be hosted on the platform, next to the bot's code.

Create the front-end with your usual tool (e.g. `npm create vite`), then run
`npx tgcloud init` (or `npm create @tgcloud/bot .`) in the same folder. It adds
`tgcloud/` next to the front-end, detects the build folder and adds a `deploy`
script to `package.json`.

`npm run deploy` builds the front-end and pushes it together with the code, in
one deploy; only changed files are uploaded.

Hosting is configured in `tgcloud.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/@tgcloud/cli/schema/tgcloud.json",
  "static": {
    "source": "dist",
    "spa": true,
    "immutable": ["/assets/*"]
  }
}
```

### Endpoints

`tgcloud/endpoints/<name>.js` is a function your Mini App calls:

```js
// tgcloud/endpoints/getProfile.js
import { EndpointError } from 'sdk';

export default async function (input, ctx) {
  const user = ctx.initData.user; // verified by the platform
  if (!user) throw new EndpointError('Not allowed');
  return { hello: user.first_name };
}
```

Call it from the Mini App with the official `telegram-web-app.js`:

```js
Telegram.WebApp.Serverless.call('getProfile', { lang: 'en' }, function (err, result) {
  if (err) return showError(err.message);
  render(result);
});
```

### Breaking: modules move to `tgcloud/`

Everything the platform runs now lives in `tgcloud/` at the project root. A regular
bot needs nothing else; the rest of the root is free for an optional Mini App
front-end.

```
my-bot/
├─ tgcloud/
│  ├─ schema.js
│  ├─ lib/
│  ├─ handlers/
│  └─ endpoints/      # optional: for a Mini App
├─ tgcloud.jsonc      # project config
├─ src/  dist/        # optional: Mini App front-end
└─ package.json
```

Module names are unchanged (`lib/cart`, `handlers/message`). To upgrade a 0.1.x
project, run once:

```sh
npx tgcloud upgrade
```

Other commands refuse to run on the old layout until you do.
